meta.task: Build a small HTTP JSON API, using only the Python standard library (no third-party dependencies), for consulting a mock database of books. Endpoints: list all books, get one book by id (return 404 if missing), and search books by author. Include unit tests.

result.summary: sources/ is empty, so there are no reference files. I read the official Python http.server documentation (opened at https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html). It confirms the API can be built with the standard library alone. The design suggestions below (routes, JSON shape, test approach) are my recommendations, not facts from a source.

findings.claim: http.server provides HTTPServer and ThreadingHTTPServer (the latter added in 3.7). Both need a RequestHandlerClass. BaseHTTPRequestHandler must be subclassed, with do_GET etc. implemented. The method name is built from the request method.

The handler's `path` attribute includes the query string, so the code must split it itself (e.g. with urllib.parse) to handle /books?author=X and /books/<id>. This follows from the documented `path` attribute. The urllib.parse suggestion is mine and I did not open that doc.

send_response(code), send_header(), and end_headers() are used to build a reply. The body is written to wfile. send_error(code, message) sends an error reply, but its default content type is text/html (error_content_type). A JSON API should write its own JSON 404 body, or override error_content_type and error_message_format.
protocol_version defaults to HTTP/1.0. If set to HTTP/1.1, every response must carry an accurate Content-Length header.
http.server is not recommended for production. Its send_header does no CRLF validation, so untrusted input must not be echoed into headers. This is fine for a mock API.

The docs show a run() pattern: build the server with a (host, port) tuple and call serve_forever(). For tests, binding to port 0 lets the OS pick a free port (my suggestion, not stated in the doc). Run the server in a thread and call shutdown() afterwards.

open_questions: Exact route shapes (/books, /books/<id>, /books?author=X or /authors/<name>/books) are not specified by the task. The team must choose.
Whether author search should be case-insensitive or substring-based is unspecified. The team must decide.
The behaviour for a non-integer id (400 or 404) is unspecified. I did not open the unittest or json docs. Those APIs are standard library but were not verified here.

result.goal: Deliver a stdlib-only Python HTTP JSON API over an in-memory mock book database, with endpoints to list books, get a book by id (404 if missing) and search by author, plus unit tests.
in_scope: Single package/module using http.server (ThreadingHTTPServer) and BaseHTTPRequestHandler, json, urllib.parse only
In-memory mock data: ~8-10 books with id (int), title, author, year
GET /books returns a JSON list of all books
GET /books/<id> returns one book; 404 JSON body {"error": ...} if the id is missing
GET /books?author=X returns the matching books; case-insensitive substring match; empty list if none match
Non-integer id returns 400 with JSON error; unknown route returns 404 JSON; non-GET methods return 405 JSON
All responses use Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and an accurate Content-Length
Own JSON error writer instead of send_error, which defaults to HTML
unittest suite: unit tests for the data/search logic, plus integration tests that start the server on port 0 in a thread and call it with urllib.request, then shut it down
Short README with run and test commands (python -m unittest)
Server entry point with host/port configurable, default 127.0.0.1:8000
milestones: 1. Fix design decisions: routes, JSON shape, status codes, search semantics, and record them in the README
2. Implement the data layer: mock books and pure functions list_books, get_book(id), search_by_author(name)
3. Implement the HTTP handler and routing, with query parsing, JSON helper and error responses, and a main() that serves
4. Write unit tests for the data layer and handler tests against a live server on an ephemeral port (200, 404 missing id, 400 bad id, author search hit, miss, case-insensitivity, unknown route, 405)
5. Run the full test suite, do a manual curl smoke test, and finalise the README
risks: http.server HTTP/1.0 vs 1.1: with HTTP/1.1 a wrong Content-Length makes clients hang; compute the length from the encoded bytes
Author names in the query need URL-decoding and may contain spaces or unicode; use parse_qs
Tests that leave the server running or use a fixed port can hang or be flaky; use port 0, shutdown() and server_close() in tearDown
Never echo user input into headers (no CRLF validation in send_header)
Handler logging clutters test output; override log_message
assumptions: The route shape /books, /books/<id>, /books?author=X is acceptable since the task does not specify one
Author search is case-insensitive substring matching
A non-integer id returns 400, a valid but unknown id returns 404
A trailing slash is tolerated or returns 404, and it is documented either way
No reference files exist in sources/, so the design relies on the official http.server docs

result.overview: A stdlib-only Python (3.7+) HTTP JSON API over an in-memory mock book database. It serves GET /books, GET /books/<id> and GET /books?author=X. It has JSON error handling and a unittest suite. Out of scope: persistence, write endpoints, auth, pagination, sorting, other filters, production hardening, TLS, third-party dependencies, OpenAPI.

requirements.text: The service uses only the Python standard library (http.server ThreadingHTTPServer/BaseHTTPRequestHandler, json, urllib.parse); no third-party dependencies.
requirements.acceptance: Static inspection of all source and test imports shows only stdlib modules; the project has no requirements/dependency file listing third-party packages; the server starts on a clean Python 3.7+ install.

result.design:
Stdlib-only book API (Python 3.7+). No dependency file is needed or allowed.

IMPORT ALLOWLIST (one shared contract for all work items)
The only top-level modules any .py file in bookapi/ or tests/ may import are listed in this set. It is the single source of truth.
ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL = {"__future__", "argparse", "ast", "contextlib", "copy", "http", "io", "json", "os", "re", "sys", "threading", "typing", "unittest", "urllib", "bookapi", "tests"}
- The set covers these submodules: http.server, urllib.parse, urllib.request, urllib.error and unittest.mock. Only the top-level name before the first dot is checked.
- W1 defines this exact set as the constant ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL in tests/test_data.py. The R1 test compares against this set only. It does not use sys.stdlib_module_names and has no other fallback.
- W2 (server.py, __main__.py, test_server.py) must not import any module outside this set. For example, use os rather than pathlib, and io.StringIO with contextlib.redirect_stderr/redirect_stdout.
- Relative imports (ImportFrom with level > 0) count as local and are allowed.
- Type hints: Python 3.7 cannot evaluate `dict | None`. Use typing.Optional/List/Dict, or put `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of the file.

LAYOUT
bookapi/__init__.py   package marker. Has a docstring and __all__ only.
bookapi/data.py       mock data plus pure functions (no I/O)
bookapi/server.py     HTTP handler, routing, JSON writer, make_server(), main()
bookapi/__main__.py   `from bookapi.server import main; raise SystemExit(main())`
tests/__init__.py     empty. Needed so `python3 -m unittest` discovery finds tests/.
tests/test_data.py    data-layer unit tests plus the R1 import check
tests/test_server.py  integration tests against a live server on port 0
README.md

DATA MODEL (bookapi/data.py)
BOOKS is a module-level tuple of 10 dicts. Each dict has exactly these keys: {"id": int, "title": str, "author": str, "year": int}.
- Ids are 1..10 and unique.
- At least 2 books share an author: "Jane Austen" x2 and "George Orwell" x2.
- One author has a non-ASCII name: "Gabriel García Márquez".

Functions:
- list_books() -> List[dict]: copies (dict(b)) of all books in id order.
- get_book(book_id: int) -> Optional[dict]: a copy of the matching book, or None.
- search_by_author(name: str) -> List[dict]: copies of the books where name.casefold() in book["author"].casefold(), in id order. An empty name matches all books. The input is not stripped.

HTTP CONTRACT (bookapi/server.py)
The server keeps the default protocol_version, HTTP/1.0, so the connection closes after each response. The path is split with urllib.parse.urlsplit(self.path). Routing is exact, with no trailing-slash tolerance.

GET "/books":
- If the query contains an author param, parse it with qs = parse_qs(query, keep_blank_values=True) and take qs["author"][0] (UTF-8 percent and + decoding). Return 200 with search_by_author(value).
- Otherwise return 200 with list_books(). Other params are ignored.

GET paths that match ^/books/([^/]+)$:
- If the segment matches ^[0-9]+$, convert it with int() and look it up. Return 200 with the book object, or 404 {"error": "Book not found"}.
- Otherwise return 400 {"error": "Invalid book id; must be a non-negative integer"}.
- The query string is ignored.

Any other GET path returns 404 {"error": "Not found"}. This includes "/books/" and "/books/1/".

POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD and OPTIONS on any path return 405 {"error": "Method not allowed"} plus the header "Allow: GET". A HEAD response sends the headers (Content-Length of the would-be body included) but no body.

A success body is the bare JSON array or object. An error body is {"error": "<fixed constant message>"}. User input never reaches headers.

class BookRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
- server_version = "BookAPI/1.0"
- _send_json(self, status, payload, extra_headers=None, include_body=True). This is the only response writer; send_error is never used.
  1. body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
  2. send_response(status)
  3. Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
  4. Content-Length: str(len(body))
  5. the extra headers
  6. end_headers()
  7. if include_body, wfile.write(body)
- _send_error_json(status, message, **kw) calls _send_json(status, {"error": message}, **kw).
- do_GET implements the routing above.
- _method_not_allowed(include_body=True) sends the 405. do_POST, do_PUT, do_DELETE, do_PATCH and do_OPTIONS call it. do_HEAD calls it with include_body=False.
- log_message(self, format, *args) is a no-op.

Module functions:
- make_server(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000) -> http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer. It binds BookRequestHandler and sets daemon_threads = True.
- main(argv=None) -> int:
  - argparse options: --host (default 127.0.0.1) and --port (int, default 8000).
  - It calls make_server(args.host, args.port) through the module-global name, so tests can monkeypatch it.
  - It prints "Serving on http://HOST:PORT" using server.server_address.
  - It calls serve_forever(). A KeyboardInterrupt is caught quietly. server_close() runs in a finally block. Returns 0.
- The module ends with an `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())` guard.

TESTS
tests/test_data.py:
- BOOKS has 8 to 10 records. Each has exactly the 4 keys with the right types; id and year are int and not bool. Ids are unique.
- list_books() equals list(BOOKS), and mutating its result does not change BOOKS.
- get_book returns the book for a hit and None for a miss.
- search_by_author:
  - exact author name
  - partial, differently cased name gives the same result
  - a miss returns []
  - "garcía" matches
- R1 import check:
  - Walk bookapi/ and tests/ with os.walk. The roots are found from os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) and its parent.
  - Parse each .py file with ast.parse (encoding utf-8).
  - For ast.Import, take alias.name.split(".")[0]. For ast.ImportFrom with level == 0, take module.split(".")[0].
  - Assert that every name found is in ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL.

tests/test_server.py (imports limited to ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL):
- setUpClass:
  - server = make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
  - port = server.server_address[1]
  - start a daemon threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
- tearDownClass: server.shutdown(), server.server_close(), thread.join(5).
- request(method, path) -> (status, headers, body_bytes). It uses urllib.request.Request plus urlopen(timeout=5) and catches urllib.error.HTTPError to get the code, headers and body.
- assert_json_headers(headers, body) checks Content-Type == "application/json; charset=utf-8" and int(Content-Length) == len(body). It runs on every response.
- Cases:
  - /books equals data.list_books()
  - /books/1 equals get_book(1)
  - /books/99999 returns 404 with a str error
  - /books/abc returns 400
  - ?author=orwell and ?author=ORWELL give the same 2 books
  - ?author=zzz returns 200 and []
  - ?author=jane%20austen and ?author=jane+austen both match 2 books
  - ?author=Garc%C3%ADa matches
  - /nope and /books/ return 404
  - POST, PUT and DELETE on /books return 405 with Allow: GET
- Silent logging: wrap one request in contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()) and assert the buffer stays empty.
- main() arguments:
  - Use unittest.mock.patch("bookapi.server.make_server") with a stub that records its args. The stub returns a fake server with server_address set, serve_forever raising KeyboardInterrupt, and server_close as a no-op.
  - main([]) calls the stub with ("127.0.0.1", 8000).
  - main(["--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "9001"]) calls it with ("0.0.0.0", 9001).
  - Both return 0. Stdout is captured with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()).

result.summary:
I updated W1 to match the revised spec. The import check now uses only the design's exact allowlist, and the full test suite passes.

- **Import allowlist in `tests/test_data.py`:**
  - I removed my wider allowlist (which had extras such as `pathlib`, `socket` and `time`) and the fallback that accepted any module in Python's own stdlib list on 3.10 and newer.
  - `ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL` is now the design's set copied exactly, with nothing added: `__future__`, `argparse`, `ast`, `contextlib`, `copy`, `http`, `io`, `json`, `os`, `re`, `sys`, `threading`, `typing`, `unittest`, `urllib`, `bookapi`, `tests`.
  - The check uses `os.walk` to go through `bookapi/` and `tests/`, finding both from the test file's own location. It parses each `.py` file and checks the first part of every absolute import name against that set. Relative imports are allowed.
  - A new test checks the set still has 17 entries.
  - The test file no longer imports `sys`.
- **Type hints in `bookapi/data.py`:** I added `typing` hints (`List`, `Optional`, `Dict`) that work on Python 3.7. The data and behaviour are unchanged: `BOOKS` is a tuple of 10 records with ids 1 to 10, Jane Austen and George Orwell twice each, and "Gabriel García Márquez". All three functions return copies, and author search is case-insensitive substring matching in id order.
- **Unchanged:** `bookapi/__init__.py` (docstring and `__all__` only) and the empty `tests/__init__.py`. The data tests still cover the dataset's shape and types, unique ids, copies, hit and miss, case-insensitive partial matching and the unicode match.

One addition the spec doesn't ask for: I kept the test that fails if a `requirements.txt`, `Pipfile` or `poetry.lock` file exists, because R1 says the project has no dependency file. W2's server and test files import only allowed modules, so they pass the stricter check.
result.tests: From the workspace root I ran `python3 -m unittest -v`: it exited with code 0, and all 47 tests passed in about 2 seconds (the data tests plus W2's server tests). I also ran `python3 -m unittest tests.test_data -v` on its own: 19 tests ran and all passed. `tests/__init__.py` is 0 bytes.

result.summary:
I checked my W2 work against the revised spec. Only one change was needed: the main() tests now replace `make_server` with `unittest.mock.patch("bookapi.server.make_server")`, as the spec now requires, instead of swapping it by hand. The full suite passes (48 tests).

**Server and entry point (unchanged):** `bookapi/server.py` and `bookapi/__main__.py` already matched the revised spec.
- **Responses:** every response, errors included, is written by `_send_json` and `_send_error_json`. Each has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and a correct `Content-Length`. `send_error` is never used.
- **Routing:**
  - `GET /books` returns all books.
  - `GET /books?author=` searches by author, decoding the value with `parse_qs(keep_blank_values=True)`.
  - `GET /books/<id>` returns the book, 400 if the id isn't all digits, or 404 if it doesn't exist.
  - Any other path returns 404, including `/books/` and `/books/1/`.
- **Other methods:** POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH and OPTIONS return 405 with `Allow: GET`. HEAD gets the same 405 headers but no body.
- **Startup:** request logging is turned off. `make_server` returns a threaded server with `daemon_threads=True`. `main(argv)` takes `--host`/`--port` (default 127.0.0.1:8000), prints `Serving on http://HOST:PORT`, stops quietly on Ctrl-C, always closes the server and returns 0.

**Changes in `tests/test_server.py`:**
- The `make_server` stand-in now records its arguments and returns a fake server. The tests check it is called with `("127.0.0.1", 8000)` for `main([])` and with `("0.0.0.0", 9001)` for the custom arguments. Both return 0, with output captured through `redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())`.
- A bad `--port` exits without calling `make_server`.
- I added one test that checks the patch replaces the module-level `make_server`, which is the name `main()` uses.

All other tests are unchanged. The only new import is `unittest.mock`, which is covered by the allowlist entry `unittest`.

result.tests:
I ran `python3 -m unittest -v` and then `python3 -m unittest` after editing; both exited 0 with all 48 tests passing.

I also checked the README's claims against a live server (`python3 -m bookapi --port 8766`). Every response matched what the README says:
- `/books/` and `/books/1/` returned 404 with `{"error": "Not found"}`.
- `/books/03` returned 200 with book 3.
- `/books/-1` returned 400 with the invalid-id message.
- `/books?author=` returned 200 with the full list.
- `/books?author=ORWELL` returned 200 with the Orwell books.

item.title: README
item.description: Write README.md covering: requirements (Python 3.7+, no dependencies); the run command `python3 -m bookapi [--host H] [--port P]` (default 127.0.0.1:8000); the test command `python3 -m unittest -v` (python -m unittest); the three endpoints (GET /books, GET /books/<id>, GET /books?author=X) with example curl calls and JSON shapes; the error body {"error": ...}; status codes 200/400/404/405 and when each occurs; search semantics (case-insensitive substring on author, URL-decoded, an empty value matches all, no match returns []); and trailing-slash behaviour (/books/ and /books/1/ return 404).
